# SGP4 reference fixtures

`vallado.txt` contains all 668 states (666 successes, 2 divergence errors) for
33 satellites in `sgp4` 2.4.0's `tests/test_cases.toml`, transcribed without
rounding into a simple text format. Source:
https://github.com/neuromorphicsystems/sgp4/blob/66b63188adf59d3351abd3d081db4683270f2d54/tests/test_cases.toml
(upstream MIT license in `LICENSE-MIT`). These are the published Vallado
SGP4-VER / `tcppver.out` results, not values generated by Siderust.
The suite includes near-Earth drag, low perigee, negative offsets, Lyddane,
geosynchronous, half-day Molniya resonance, extreme eccentricity and decaying
trajectories. It includes the three downstream spod regressions and extends
them to the complete reference set.

`iau.txt` contains 48 independently calculated improved-mode vectors for
WGS-72/IAU and WGS-84/IAU at -1440, 0, 1440 and 4320 minutes for six satellites
from the same corpus (00005, 04632, 08195, 24208, 26900, 28623). Generated with
python-sgp4 2.25's Vallado **C++** extension (`Satrec.twoline2rv`, default improved
mode), independently of Siderust. Source: https://github.com/brandon-rhodes/python-sgp4/tree/2.25
(MIT license in `LICENSE-python-sgp4`). Reproduce from the repository root:

```sh
uv run --python 3.12 --with sgp4==2.25 tests/fixtures/sgp4/generate_iau.py
```

`synthetic.txt` adds 315 independent C++ vectors for all three model modes.
These isolate half-day eccentricity-polynomial boundaries, low inclinations,
zero eccentricity, retrograde orbits, the 225-minute regime boundary, fractional
negative offsets and positive/negative drag. Error code 6 (sub-Earth radius) is
retained as a numerical state, matching the documented reference contract.
The same generator reproduces this file.

All successful vectors are checked via the typed Siderust API with absolute
component errors strictly below **1e-6 km** and **1e-9 km/s**. No relaxed
numerical-vector tolerances are used. Round trips from the resulting typed UTC
epoch use the same limits. FFI tests compare the identical scalar UTC request
against the typed API exactly, avoiding any hidden tolerance for scalar JD loss.

The C++ reference generator is only a fixture maintenance tool; Python and its
sgp4 package are not build or test dependencies.
